name: MimiClaw
vibe_summary: An OpenClaw-style AI assistant squeezed onto a $5 ESP32-S3 chip with no OS, no Node.js, and pure C. It talks over Telegram, keeps local memory on flash, and sips 0.5W of power.

Users who want a Telegram assistant with local flash memory
avoid_if: You need a rich plugin ecosystem or desktop integrations
You want multi-channel support beyond Telegram/Feishu
You are not comfortable flashing embedded firmware

No OS or runtime dependencies — pure C bare metal
All data stored locally on device flash
Extremely fast boot and tiny footprint

Constrained by 8MB PSRAM and 16MB flash limits

overview_markdown:
MimiClaw is a bare-metal reimagining of the OpenClaw personal AI assistant, running entirely on a $5 ESP32-S3 microcontroller with no operating system, no Node.js, and no Linux — just pure C built on ESP-IDF. You message it via Telegram (or Feishu), the chip polls over WiFi, runs an agent loop against Anthropic Claude or OpenAI GPT (switchable at runtime), calls tools, reads memory, and replies — all while drawing about 0.5W from a USB port.

Its architecture is strikingly minimal: session memory persists on local SPIFFS flash, the firmware ships as a single merged image with CI-built releases, and recent work added GPIO skill support, group-chat mention filtering to avoid wasted LLM calls, and USB-JTAG console access for web-based serial monitoring. Compared to OpenClaw's full desktop/server stack with a control UI and dozens of integrations, MimiClaw trades ecosystem breadth for radical portability, cost, and energy efficiency — a genuinely 'hardware agent OS' for the edge.
